articles.title: AQI slips to 'severe' in Delhi; Mumbai, Chennai wake up to smog morning after Deepavali
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Delhi Air Quality Index slips near “severe” mark as a thick layer of toxic haze engulfed India’s National capital on Monday (November 9, 2026). Despite stringent restrictions on fireworks imposed by the Supreme Court, people defied the deadline way past 10 p.m. on Deepavali night.
According to the Central Pollution Control Board Live Dashboard, Delhi AQI levels have gone up to 404 at 4 a.m. today and have been in respite since then.

Burari Crossing registered the highest reading at 441, followed by Vivek Vihar at 437, Delhi Technological University (DTU) at 434, North Campus of Delhi University and Jahangirpuri at 433 each, and Rohini at 430.
Beyond the National Capital, AQI also slumped in several other Indian cities. Mumbai saw hazy conditions, with a thick layer of smog blanketing the Kalanagar and Bandra areas as air quality worsened.

According to monitoring data, Kherwadi-Bandra East recorded an AQI of 264, followed by Sewri at 226, Ghatkopar at 221 and Chembur at 216. Byculla recorded an AQI of 193, Mindspace-Malad West 191, Kandivali West 187 and Worli 148. Kurla recorded an AQI of 96.
In Uttar Pradesh, a thick layer of smog blanketed Lucknow as several parts of the city woke up to hazy conditions.

Northern and western hubs bore the brunt of the pollution, with Lucknow (246), Amritsar (242), Jodhpur (234), Ahmedabad (230), Dehradun (228), Jaipur (223), Udaipur (223), and Surat (207) all slipping into the “poor” category.
Central and industrial belts similarly saw a spike in readings, including Nagpur (239), Pune (221), Bhopal (205), Mumbai (171) and Kolkata (167), exacerbated by Deepavali emissions.

Meanwhile, southern cities maintained relatively cleaner profiles, with Chennai standing at 208 (”poor”), while Bangalore (127), Hyderabad (120) and Thiruvananthapuram (67) recorded moderate-to-satisfactory air quality levels.
According to CPCB classification, an AQI between 0 and 50 is considered ‘good’, 51-100 ‘satisfactory’, 101-200 ‘moderate’, 201-300 ‘poor’, 301-400 ‘very poor’ and 401-500 ‘severe’.

With Stage III measures in force following the CAQM’s decision, existing restrictions will continue alongside additional pollution-control measures, increased enforcement and directions to concerned agencies to prevent further deterioration in air quality.

The emergency action plan applies across Delhi and adjoining districts of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan. It is invoked as a precautionary measure based on meteorological and pollution forecasts provided by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) and the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), allowing restrictions to be implemented before citywide AQI levels reach the ‘severe’ category.

Police identified the victims as S. Rahul (17) and R. Vishal (17) — both of Inam Samayapuram village in Manachanallur taluk. The victims were relatives and engaged in garland making work at Samayapuram.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Deepavali night (November 8, 2026) in Delhi saw air pollution levels in the national capital reach alarmingly high levels after firecrackers were burst across the city well past the Supreme Court-permitted hours on the festival. The national capital is under Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) with multiple restrictions in place.

A row has now been sparked after senior Congress leader Ajay Maken flagged the non-availability of PM 2.5 readings at 25 of Delhi’s 39 air quality monitoring stations on the night of Deepavali. He pointed out that air pollution levels at the national capital’s nine stations reached 38.4 times the World Health Organisation’s (WHO) 24-hour limit (as per available data)

Mr Maken, in a post on X, alleged discrepancies in the capital’s air pollution monitoring data, claiming that PM 2.5 readings in 25 stations were not recorded between 2 AM and 3 AM on the night of the festival.

“The government which shuts down air quality monitoring stations on the night of Diwali, the government that does data fraud, how will you trust such a government?” asked AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj in a video posted on X.

Particulate matter, or particle pollution , is the general term for a mixture of solid particles and liquid droplets found in the air. A wide range of minute particles in the air can be seen only with an electron microscope. It includes sulphates, nitrates, black carbon, particle-bound water, metals (cadmium, copper, nickel, zinc) and hydrocarbons. In addition, biological components such as allergens (pollen, dust mites) and microbial compounds (fungi) are also considered to be particulate matter.
There are two sizes of particulate matter (PM), i.e. PM 10 and PM 2.5.

articles.title: Hyderabad: Retired banker’s sketch puts Ladki-Ka-Pul’s one-way traffic plan in motion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A 73-year-old retired bank employee’s hand-drawn map has given Hyderabad Traffic Police an idea they are now seriously examining — a one-way traffic loop around Lakdi-ka-pul and Saifabad. What began as an email suggestion nearly a year ago has progressed to a traffic simulation study and inspections by senior police officers, even as the department explores similar arrangements at other congestion-prone locations across Hyderabad.

Palakodeti Chandrasekhar emailed the police with his proposal to reorganise traffic movement in the busy Lakdi-ka-pul stretch. He was subsequently invited to the Police Commissioner’s office, where he explained the idea. Mr. Chandrasekhar also submitted a hand-drawn map, marking the proposed directions of traffic with arrows.
“I am neither a police officer nor an engineer, and I am certainly no expert at drawing. I sketched the map to the best of my ability,” Mr. Chandrasekhar said.

The sketch maps a proposed loop connecting Lakdi-ka-pul, the Secretariat road, Ravindra Bharathi and the Old Saifabad Police Station, with landmarks such as Dwaraka Hotel, the LIC Building, the Assembly, Public Gardens and the DGP’s office marked along the route.
A view of traffic on Lakdi-ka-pul stretch in Hyderabad. File | Photo Credit: NAGARA GOPAL

Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic) D. Joel Davis said the police had conducted a simulation study to assess its feasibility. However, several road improvements would be necessary before even a trial could be introduced. “Certain intersections would have to be developed or modified to ensure smoother movement under the proposed arrangement,” said the officer.

Hyderabad Police Commissioner V.C. Sajjanar, accompanied by Mr. Davis; DCP Traffic-I Avinash Kumar; ACP Traffic Khairatabad Zone S. Mohan Kumar and Traffic Adviser Venkat Ramaiah, inspected stretches near Dwaraka Hotel, the Old Saifabad Police Station, HDFC, Iqbal Minar and Ravindra Bharathi to assess road conditions and existing traffic patterns.

Mr. Sajjanar said that one-way loops might require motorists to travel a few hundred metres extra, but could make journeys hassle-free, reduce honking and help curb pollution caused by congestion and vehicles remaining stationary with their engines running.

Referring to the one-way arrangement around KBR Park , he said the police had received considerable positive feedback from commuters, particularly about smoother movement and reduced honking. He said there was hardly any honking around KBR Park following the changes. “There were some hiccups initially, but I thank the people of Hyderabad for supporting the initiative. We look forward to better collaboration between the public and the police,” he said.
Hyderabad Police received positive feedback from people about one-way vehicular flow around Kasu Brahmananda Reddy (KBR) National Park in Hyderabad. File | Photo Credit: NAGARA GOPAL

In Cyberabad, officials are examining a separate loop connecting Biodiversity Junction, IKEA , Mindspace Rotary, Times Square Road, Knowledge City, Qualcomm, Dallas Centre Road and My Home Bhooja, before reconnecting with Biodiversity Junction.

Cyberabad Commissioner of Police M. Ramesh and Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Sunpreet Singh inspected the proposed corridor on November 6. Officials were asked to prepare a detailed traffic study covering bottlenecks, traffic generated by buildings and the availability and capacity of parking facilities.

articles.title: Keralam power purchase row: BJP leader V. Muraleedharan says CM must clarify if tenders were called
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national executive member and MLA V. Muraleedharan has asked Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan to clarify whether tenders were invited before the government opted to purchase power from GNA Energy, a digital over-the-counter (OTC) trading platform.

Stressing the need for transparency in the use of government funds at a press conference on Monday, Mr. Muraleedharan said the government should also clarify whether private companies other than GNA Energy had approached it and the rates offered by them.

The “power crisis” in the State, he said, was felt most acutely during peak hours, from 6 p.m. to midnight or 2 a.m. However, the agreement with GNA Energy was for the purchase of power round the clock, and not just during peak hours. According to experts, this would create an additional burden of ₹1,500 crore on the people, he said.

Mr. Muraleedharan asked whether the government would be willing to disclose a comparison of the peak-hour power supply offered by GNA Energy and the Himachal Pradesh government, along with the rates, “in a manner that can be understood by the layman.”

Keralam experienced the highest power shortage during April and May. However, the agreement with GNA Energy covered the period from November 2026 to March 2027. Negotiations for power purchases for April and May would see a further increase in rates. However, the rates offered by Himachal Pradesh covered the April-May period as well. “What is the rationale behind declining Himachal Pradesh’s offer and going with GNA Energy without inviting tenders?” the senior BJP leader asked.
If tenders were not invited, the government should clarify what other norms were followed in selecting GNA Energy, he added.

He also questioned why Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph was silent on the issue. “Does he have no stance on the issue? Usually, it is the Electricity Department that takes decisions on such matters. However, recently the Chief Minister has been making statements on the matter. Has the Electricity Minister gone on leave? Is the Chief Minister handling his portfolio?” Mr. Muraleedharan asked.
The MLA said there were suspicions that the Kerala State Electricity Regulatory Commission was being overruled when such decisions were made.
He also questioned why the United Democratic Front (UDF) government in Keralam was not entering into an agreement with another Congress-ruled State and was instead opting for GNA Energy.
The Chief Minister recently defended his decision to accept GNA Energy’s offer over a proposal from Himachal Pradesh, stating that the latter would entail an additional liability of ₹2,230 crore.

articles.title: Excess ethanol in petrol: Keralam launches random checks at pumps after Karnataka detects high levels
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: After sample testing in Karnataka revealed that petrol sold by several major oil companies in the State contained ethanol far above the prescribed 20% level , the Keralam government has also begun inspections in fuel outlets to check ethanol levels. Food and Civil Supplies Minister Anoop Jacob on Monday (November 9, 2026) announced random inspections at fuel outlets in four districts – Thiruvananthapuram, Ernakulam, Kozhikode and Kannur.

Thiruvananthapuram District Supply Officer Smitha S.R. told The Hindu that samples are being collected from two pumps in the district, which will be sent to a lab accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) for analysis.
“We have completed a sample collection from one of the pumps. Samples from one more pump will be collected today (Monday),” she said.

In samples collected in Karnataka, the level of ethanol in some cases was found to be as high as 31.2%, raising questions about transparency in the ethanol-blended petrol being sold to consumers across the country. The Commissioner of Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs as well as Taluk Supply Officers have the powers to conduct inspections and initiate legal action as per a 2014 notification issued by the State government.
Mr. Jacob said the sample analysis will be completed in a timebound manner, with results expected within 10 days.

He said the government decided to go ahead with the inspections considering the developments in Karnataka as well as the complaints and concerns raised by consumers regarding possible damage to their vehicles due to contaminated fuel.

articles.title: Oil falls as Donald Trump says new Iran attacks ‘unlikely’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Oil prices fell at Monday’s (November 9, 2026) open after U.S. President ​Donald Trump said he was highly unlikely to order new Iran ‌attackswhile talks to end the conflict make progress, despite both ​nations’ reports of attacks on ships in or near ⁠the Strait of Hormuz.
Brent was down 84 cents, or 0.85%, to $97.48 a barrel by 0138 GMT, while West Texas Intermediate fell 32 cents, or ‌0.35%, to $90.51 a barrel.

The fall reversed minor gains made on Friday’s (November 6, 2026) settlement as the market assessed the ‌possibility of further U.S. strikes on Iran, although Brent fell ‌17% ⁠last week, the steepest weekly drop since the start ⁠of the COVID pandemic and the biggest in absolute terms, according to LSEG data dating back to 1988.
“It depends on whether or not they sign ​a very strong agreement,” Trump ‌told CNN in a phone interview. “The answer is, highly unlikely it’s going to be necessary.”

Mr. Trump had hinted at renewing attacks on Iran after last week’s U.S. midterm elections , but there has ‌been no sign of a large-scale U.S. military operation. ​Iran has said it would respond by striking U.S. and Israeli targets.

Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM ⁠Trade, called Mr. Trump’s comments “more measured” but said “the market is still waiting to see whether the midterms have produced a lasting shift in Trump’s ‌approach to the conflict, or whether this is just another temporary change in tone.”

articles.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

For a few weeks, Rampur, on the banks of the Sutlej river, comes alive with the fair (November 11-14 this year, with trading grounds open through the month), offering a sensory map of the Himalaya. Colourful textiles, yak wool, pashmina, dry fruits, agricultural produce, Kinnauri apples, indigenous crafts and precious stones fill the marketplace. Among its most captivating sights are the magnificent Chamurthi horses, the hardy “ships of the cold desert”.
Kinnauri weaves on sale at Lavi Fair. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala
At the Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, Shimla district. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala
Jewellery on sale at Lavi Fair. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala

Traders once travelled from Tibet, Nepal, Central Asia and Afghanistan. Tradition traces the fair’s origins to a 17th-century treaty between Raja Kehri Singh of Bushahr and Tibet, establishing it as a meeting point for traders, pilgrims and storytellers along the Silk Route. Though trans-Himalayan trade declined after Tibet’s occupation in 1959, the fair survived on the Buddhist circuit and was accorded international status by the Himachal Pradesh government.

Pratibha Singh, a member of the Rampur Bushahr royal family which founded the fair and continues to honour the tradition, recalls its legacy of pashmina and Kinnauri shawls, some woven over years, alongside trans-Himalayan textiles and local produce. The GI-tagged Kinnauri shawl, with bright geometric motifs, speaks its own language of colour: white for water, yellow for earth, red for fire, green for air, and blue for sky.

On my last visit, a group of elderly women from South India told me they discovered the fair through a fellow traveller whose husband was a biker in the 1990s. A friend from Odisha recalls how in the 90s, his ophthalmologist-father’s eye camps in Rampur led to lifelong friendships and an annual habit of sourcing Kinnauri apples and dry fruits.
Kinnauri apples on sale at Lavi Fair. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala
Traders at Lavi Fair accept payments via UPI now. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala

For Ami Chand Gautam, a Lavi trader since the 1980s, the fair tells a story of changing prices and livelihoods. He remembers when “ chilgoza , the rare pine nut gathered in Kinnaur’s upper reaches, sold for just ₹4-₹5 per kg, almost the price of rice then. Today, it fetches ₹14,000-15,000 per kg,” he says.

articles.title: Amid price rise, Centre mandates rice, paddy stock declaration
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: With rice prices rising due to a deficient and uneven monsoon, the Centre on Friday (November 7, 2026) directed traders, retailers, wholesalers, processors and millers across the country to declare their rice and paddy stocks and allowed five southern States to impose stock limits to prevent hoarding.

Under a November 6 order, all traders and wholesalers, retailers, large retail chains and processors and millers in all States and Union Territories must declare stocks under six categories — Basmati rice, non-Basmati premium rice, non-Basmati rice, parboiled rice, broken rice and paddy.
Every unit holding stocks will have to update details on the Food Stock Portal (foodstock.dfpd.gov.in) every Friday, the Food Ministry said in a statement.
Units that are not registered on the portal or that violate stock limits will face action under Sections 6 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.

In a separate letter, also dated November 6, the Centre has given its consent to Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana to impose stock limits on paddy and rice through control orders.

The limits will remain in force till January 31, 2027. The Centre and States will monitor implementation to ensure adequate availability and prevent hoarding and black marketing, an official statement said.

To improve availability, the Centre is allocating additional rice stocks to NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar for sale as Bharat Rice, and has asked them to explore all possible distribution channels, especially in the southern States.

The Centre has also doubled the target for rice sales through e-auction under the Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic) for 2026-27 from 25 lakh tonnes to 50 lakh tonnes. Around 25 lakh tonnes had been sold to private parties by October 31, compared to 11 lakh tonnes in the same period of the last year.
Trade and industry experts said deficient and uneven rainfall had contributed to rice inflation, particularly in premium non-Basmati varieties, and pushed up paddy prices in several markets.
Retail rice inflation rose to 8.25% year-on-year in September from 5.89% in August, with the average retail price at around ₹48.23 per kg, about 12% higher than a year earlier.
Experts, however, said the situation was not a nationwide crisis.
With government rice stocks at comfortable levels, they said, pressure was sharpest in regions and grades where supplies were tight.

articles.title: China dismisses a spy plot claim involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as smear campaign
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: China denied on Monday (November 9, 2026) there was a spy plot attempt to ensnare Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, calling the spying allegations unsubstantiated and a smear campaign against Beijing.

Mr. Huang has acknowledged to the Nvidia board that he had been intimate with a business executive who U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing, according to The New York Times.
“The so-called Chinese spy allegation is unsubstantiated. It is nothing but smears against China,” Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Monday (November 9, 2026).

The chips company CEO is at the center of a controversy over whether he drove sales of advanced computer chips to China, in spite of U.S. tech restrictions aimed at limiting China’s ability to access these advanced technologies. Nvidia is one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies, alongside Apple and Microsoft.
Nvidia said on Sunday (November 8) that the company would launch an investigation into the case. Mr. Huang did not name the person in the extramarital affair.

China had previously denied the New York Times report that said Mr. Huang had developed a close relationship with a Chinese citizen named Alice Huang, who ran a company that faced claims of smuggling advanced chips into China, and that she was a spy for Beijing.

“The key questions are whether he was aware of any espionage activities and whether any confidential or strategically sensitive information was compromised,” said George Chen, a partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, a Washington-based consultancy.
“Those questions require evidence rather than speculation,” he added in written comments.

Mr. Huang had pushed to loosen chip sales restrictions to China in recent years, successfully lobbying U.S. President Donald Trump to allow his company to sell H200 chips this year. However, it is uncertain if Beijing would allow Chinese companies to buy these chips en masse.

While those chips are not Nvidia's most cutting-edge models, they are still advanced. Previously, Mr. Huang also lobbied Mr. Trump to sell the less-advanced H20 chips, which were designed for the Chinese market while complying with U.S. export restrictions.

Chinese media have largely focused on Huang admitting to the affair and state media outlets have mainly echoed the official government line. Some have said the New York Times report was aimed at destabilising U.S.-China relations.
“Whenever China-U.S. relations begin to improve, there are often those firing shots from the shadows,” the state-owned Global Times said.

fullParagraphs: Twenty people have died over the weekend trying to reach Greece’s island of Crete, which has become a main destination for migrants headed for the European Union, authorities said on Monday (November 9, 2026).
Eight bodies were found on one boat and 12 on another, while some 40 people were rescued off both, the Greek Coast Guard said on Monday (November 9).
Maritime police launched an emergency rescue late Saturday (November 7) after a boat issued an alarm signal, with strong winds making sea conditions difficult, the Coast Guard said.

Around 28 survivors and one body, all Sudanese nationals, were picked up by another boat sailing nearby, then transferred to a police vessel and taken to Crete, authorities had said on Sunday (November 8).
During the night from Sunday (November 8) to Monday (November 9), the Coast Guard found their boat, with seven additional bodies on board, it said.
In a separate incident, 12 bodies were found on a boat south of the island on Monday (November 9), while 18 people were rescued, the Coast Guard said.
Crete has become one of the main entry points into the EU for migrants departing from Libya and attempting the dangerous crossing to Greece.
Many of the attempted crossings turn deadly when the vessels sink or run into trouble.

articles.title: World entering ‘age of climate extremes’: UN chief
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The world is entering a new reality where climate extremes are the norm, the United Nations chief Antonio Guterres warned on Monday (November 9, 2026), urging leaders at the COP31 climate conference in Turkiye to “get serious”.
“A supersized El Nino is colliding with a planet already superheated by manmade climate change,” the UN secretary general said in a statement.

As leaders gathered in Antalya for the UN climate summit, Mr. Guterres called on them to “get serious by cutting emissions faster, accelerating a just transition from fossil fuels and delivering the finance and protection vulnerable countries need”.
His statement came as the UN’s World Meteorological Organization released a report indicating that 2026 has continued a streak of exceptional global temperatures, melting ice and rising sea levels.
Each of the past 12 years have been among the hottest 12 years on record, the agency said, with this year expected to be among the hottest ever.

“What we are seeing gives new meaning to the phrase off the charts,” WMO chief Celeste Saulo told reporters in Geneva, cautioning that the current exceptionally strong El Nino could unleash more heat and extreme weather well into next year.
“We should prepare for another record-breaking year in 2027.”
The global average surface temperature between January and September this year was around 1.47 degrees Celsius above the pre-industrial average, the WMO said.
And this year’s El Nino — expected to be the strongest since 1950 at least — could push the figure higher by the end of the year.

Preliminary data shows 2026 figuring among the four hottest years on record, WMO climate information chief John Kenned told reporters, adding though that “with the El Nina developing, we might see when the final numbers come in that we’re close to the top”.

fullParagraphs: The High Commission of Bangladesh has received a request from deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina seeking a fresh passport, a source in Dhaka has informed. The official has said that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Bangladesh is in the process of verifying the letter and will take a decision after internal consultation. Ms. Hasina’s passport was cancelled soon after she escaped to India in August 2024 after an uprising that toppled her government.

“We have received an email from Matrix Chambers, a law firm in London seeking a new passport for Sheikh Hasina. We are currently examining the content of the letter and will take an appropriate step after internal consultation,” said the source speaking to The Hindu over phone.

Ms. Hasina held a press conference on August 5 this year at the Foreign Correspondents Club where she had expressed her plans to return to Bangladesh in December. The announcement was followed by repeated assertion by the Awami League’s leaders who are based in India that Ms. Hasina will act on her announcement. As per sources in Awami League, Ms. Hasina may choose to return through one of the land ports with India including Benapole-Petrapole.

Ms Hasina has been living in New Delhi since being overthrown in a student-people uprising in 2024 July-August. The movement started against the abolition of quota system that ensured employment for families of the guerrillas of the 1971 Liberation War.

The movement escalated and turned into a protest against Ms. Hasina after a police crackdown in mid-July 2024 led to death of hundreds of students and common citizens ultimately leading to her escape on August 5 that year. The International Crimes Tribunal, a special tribunal that was constituted in November 2025 delivered a death sentence for Ms. Hasina. The verdict was however criticised later as it was passed without representation from Ms. Hasina or her legal team.

Ms. Hasina has so far refused to apologise for the police crackdown. In a written interview with The Hindu earlier this year, she said, “When police are working in the field, how can they contact the Prime Minister for every action? Police operate under standard operating procedures. They are trained to handle emergencies, crowd control and violent situations. When police personnel were attacked and killed, and police stations were set on fire, they responded according to the situation. How could I personally order officers in those circumstances? The police handle such situations under their SOP.”

articles.title: Nvidia investigating reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Nvidia is opening an investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort,” the company's board of directors said Sunday (November 8, 2026).

The announcement came after Mr. Huang acknowledged to the board that he had been intimate with a business executive whom U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing, The New York Times reported.

Mr. Huang apologised in a message to the company, according to the Times . “I was unfaithful to my wife,” he said. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

Nvidia's board said in a statement it has “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised,” but that its inquiry would examine all available information. Mr. Huang “fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it,” the board said.
Mr. Huang, 63, will remain CEO during the investigation.

The Times reported last month that U.S. intelligence agencies had discovered that Mr. Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, and determined that she was feeding information directly to Beijing. The two are not related, according to the Times .

Ms. Alice Huang was previously a television reporter in China before becoming a top executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, which has become one of Nvidia's biggest customers in Southeast Asia. Megaspeed bought more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the past two years, according to the Times .

articles.title: China dismisses a spy plot claim involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as smear campaign
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: China denied on Monday (November 9, 2026) there was a spy plot attempt to ensnare Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, calling the spying allegations unsubstantiated and a smear campaign against Beijing.

Mr. Huang has acknowledged to the Nvidia board that he had been intimate with a business executive who U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing, according to The New York Times.
“The so-called Chinese spy allegation is unsubstantiated. It is nothing but smears against China,” Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Monday (November 9, 2026).

The chips company CEO is at the center of a controversy over whether he drove sales of advanced computer chips to China, in spite of U.S. tech restrictions aimed at limiting China’s ability to access these advanced technologies. Nvidia is one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies, alongside Apple and Microsoft.
Nvidia said on Sunday (November 8) that the company would launch an investigation into the case. Mr. Huang did not name the person in the extramarital affair.

China had previously denied the New York Times report that said Mr. Huang had developed a close relationship with a Chinese citizen named Alice Huang, who ran a company that faced claims of smuggling advanced chips into China, and that she was a spy for Beijing.

“The key questions are whether he was aware of any espionage activities and whether any confidential or strategically sensitive information was compromised,” said George Chen, a partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, a Washington-based consultancy.
“Those questions require evidence rather than speculation,” he added in written comments.

Mr. Huang had pushed to loosen chip sales restrictions to China in recent years, successfully lobbying U.S. President Donald Trump to allow his company to sell H200 chips this year. However, it is uncertain if Beijing would allow Chinese companies to buy these chips en masse.

While those chips are not Nvidia's most cutting-edge models, they are still advanced. Previously, Mr. Huang also lobbied Mr. Trump to sell the less-advanced H20 chips, which were designed for the Chinese market while complying with U.S. export restrictions.

Chinese media have largely focused on Huang admitting to the affair and state media outlets have mainly echoed the official government line. Some have said the New York Times report was aimed at destabilising U.S.-China relations.
“Whenever China-U.S. relations begin to improve, there are often those firing shots from the shadows,” the state-owned Global Times said.

fullParagraphs: It is the dream of every (or most) digital native, or all of us living through the Information Age, to break the internet. Turns out, the answer is a resounding yes. But no, it wasn’t a celebrity posting about their latest life update, creating ripples across the globe. articles.title: Air pollution over 66 times WHO limit in parts of Delhi as people defy ban on firecrackers on Deepavali
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: As Delhiites burst firecrackers well past the 10 p.m. deadline set by the Supreme Court for Deepavali night, PM2.5 levels in parts of the city soared to 66 times the World Health Organization’s (WHO) recommended 24-hour guideline, before gradually declining in the early hours of Monday (November 9, 2026), according to official data.

However, at the peak of pollution following the bursting of firecrackers on Sunday (November 8) night, data from several monitoring stations operated by the Delhi Government’s Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) were unavailable for hours. This raises the possibility that the actual spike in pollution could have been higher.

Data was unavailable for several hours at multiple stations, including Anand Vihar, R.K. Puram, and Bawana, according to the DPCC website. Data from some other stations had also not been updated since Sunday (November 8) night.
Deepavali 2026: All you need to know about Supreme Court-permitted time slots, green crackers and other directives

According to DPCC data, the PM2.5 concentration in Punjabi Bagh stood at 993 micrograms per cubic metre at 4 a.m. on Monday (November 9) — about 66.2 times the WHO’s recommended 24-hour guideline of 15 micrograms per cubic metre.

In Vivek Vihar, the PM2.5 concentration was 873 micrograms per cubic metre at 2 a.m. on Monday (November 9), about 58.2 times the WHO guideline. In R.K. Puram, it stood at 924 micrograms per cubic metre at 10 p.m. on Sunday (November 8), about 61.6 times the guideline.

PM2.5 refers to fine inhalable particulate matter measuring 2.5 micrometres or less in diameter. These particles can penetrate deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream, potentially causing respiratory and other health problems.

Although the Supreme Court had permitted only green firecrackers during specified time windows on November 7 and 8, traditional firecrackers, which are more polluting, were also available in Delhi markets.

Delhi’s overall air quality remained in the ‘very poor’ category on Monday (November 9) morning, while several parts of the city continued to record ‘severe’ pollution levels, according to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data.
‘Severe’ air pollution affects healthy people and can seriously impact those with existing diseases, the CPCB says.

Delhi’s 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 370, in the ‘very poor’ category, at 9 a.m. on Monday. However, several areas, including Chandni Chowk, ITO, Delhi University’s North Campus, Rohini and Mundka, recorded ‘severe’ air quality.

Every winter, air pollution levels rise across Delhi-NCR and parts of the wider Indo-Gangetic Plain, largely due to meteorological conditions such as low wind speeds and falling temperatures. Emissions from stubble burning in October and November, along with firecracker use during the festive season, add to pollution from vehicles and dust, further deteriorating air quality.

C ome November, the Indo-Gangetic Plain is often clouded in a pall of pollution. The cessation of monsoon winds from the preceding four months and a drop in temperatures lead to pollutants from year-round sources, such as vehicles, power plants, construction dust and other suspended particulate matter, persisting as a black shroud because of the formation of an ‘inversion layer’. This means that these particles aren’t ‘flushed out’ from the region by the stronger winds at the higher atmospheric reaches. Add to this the contribution of stubble burning. Particulate matter from the burning of farm stubble — rice chaff — by farmers in Punjab, and to a smaller extent Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh — is added to this haze, worsening the already noxious air quality in Delhi and several other north Indian cities. Farm stubble is burnt in October and November because it is the cheapest method employed by farmers to prepare their soil for Rabi wheat.

articles.title: Supreme Court terms vehicular emissions major contributor to air pollution in Delhi-NCR
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) termed vehicular emissions a major contributor to air pollution in Delhi-NCR and said immediate, medium- and long-term measures were needed to curb the rising air quality index.

Hearing a suo motu case examining the regulatory framework governing air pollution, a Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana also expressed concern over “bumper-to-bumper” traffic in Delhi-NCR.
“We keep talking and sometimes make statements and suggestions, but the point is that AQI is already touching 400,” the CJI said.
The Bench highlighted the large number of vehicles plying on roads connecting Delhi with neighbouring areas, including Ghaziabad, Greater Noida, Gurugram and Faridabad.
“Look at the roads in Delhi and the roads connecting Delhi with the NCR. Take a look at any road and the kind of vehicles moving on it. That is the major problem,” the CJI said.
The Bench said the poor people are the real sufferers, as they are on the roads, and moreover, the festival time is the only period when they earn a livelihood.

articles.title: Epic failures: on electoral roll, welfare
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

Not every citizen is an eligible voter, and tying benefits to the electoral roll is illogical and also cruel. In West Bengal, lakhs were deleted from the rolls , many for dubious “logical discrepancies”. In the appeals heard for reinstatement, 93% resulted in the restoration of names by September 2026, pointing to massive pre-election disenfranchisement. The Court has stated that it is yet to adjudicate on the legality of the ECI’s “logical discrepancies” method. The SIR was designed by the ECI to restrict enrolment through stringent residency criteria; thus, itinerant voters had to prove their eligibility. The Opposition, civil society and even some of the BJP’s allies have objected to this, but the BJP refuses to acknowledge the SIR’s flaws. This is partly because it has benefited from disenfranchisement — as in West Bengal. But the Minister’s remarks suggest another reason. The BJP-led coalition sees the pruned electoral rolls as a way to limit welfare, especially at a time when growth in tax revenues has slowed because of the Centre’s policies. Inordinately delaying the Census, changing the procedure to appoint Election Commissioners, who then run an exercise that disenfranchises millions by design, and now, using the resultant rolls to decide who gets welfare, all cut at the heart of the painstakingly built constitutional welfare state. The sooner the Court decides the petitions against the SIR, and reiterates that its rolls cannot be used to curtail welfare, the better.

articles.title: Young and fast: on F1’s youngest champion
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Andrea Kimi Antonelli etched his name in motorsport history by becoming the youngest driver to win a Formula One World Championship . The 20-year-old has secured his maiden title with four races to spare after finishing third at the Mexico Grand Prix on Sunday. The Italian’s feat is remarkable, for he has claimed the crown in his sophomore campaign, becoming only the fifth driver in history to do so in the first or second season. Mercedes signed Antonelli for its junior driver programme when he was just 12. Since then, the Italian’s step towards F1 has been meticulously managed. After acing the F4 championships, Antonelli skipped one level to transition to F2. And when the opportunity arose to fill a seat vacated by seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff took a bold gamble by drafting in the youngster. Antonelli’s rookie campaign in 2025 was baptism by fire, and he was outclassed by teammate George Russell. For 2026, F1 ushered in drastic changes with new engine and aerodynamic regulations, dramatically altering the dynamics of the cars. Though conventional wisdom suggested that the experienced Russell would be the favourite, the Italian prodigy embraced the challenge astonishingly well. This was best exemplified by how he won five consecutive races starting from the second round of the season.

One of the hardest things in F1 is handling the nerves associated with protecting the lead, especially when it is the driver’s first attempt at a Championship bid. Antonelli, though, was incredibly consistent throughout the year, and hardly made any errors. Titles are often decided by how a driver minimises his losses on bad days, and Antonelli showed great temperament in this regard. At the same time, he was ruthless on the track and made decisive overtaking manoeuvres. The defining race was in Monza, Italy, in September, where Antonelli charged from 19th on the grid to win his home Grand Prix, finishing ahead of Russell who started second. It was a statement of intent, and strengthened his grip on the trophy. Drivers often raise their games following a world title, more so when success comes early in their career. Considering the giant leap Antonelli made to become F1’s first champion to be born in the 21st century, he will undoubtedly attract a new generation of fans. The charm of the sport lies in its iconic driver rivalries such as Ayrton Senna versus Alain Prost, and Michael Schumacher versus Mika Hakkinen. With four-time champion Max Verstappen widely considered the gold standard of the present era, Antonelli could well be the perfect candidate to battle the Dutchman in F1’s next great rivalry.

articles.title: Trump debacle: On the U.S. midterm election results
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: President Donald Trump faced the worst political setback of his current term in office after the Republican Party lost control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the mid-term election. Democrats not only won resoundingly in their traditional stronghold States, such as Colorado, Oregon and Illinois, and held onto important swing States, such as Georgia, Michigan and Virginia, but they also made historic inroads into “red states” such as Texas, Kansas and Iowa. While Mr. Trump fumed that Republicans would have performed better had his name been on the ballot, he also appeared to be resigned to the imminent reality of working with Democratic lawmakers over the remaining two years of his administration. Beyond the immediate impact on the future functioning of the federal government, this week’s “bluenami” has also brought sweeping changes at the State level: Democrats won a Senate seat in Texas for the first time in 37 years; Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won in Michigan , making him the first Muslim Senator in history ; Chris Pappas of New Hampshire became the first openly gay man to be elected to the Senate ; and Senate Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries will soon be the first African-American Speaker of the House.
Federal judge orders 14-day delay on any work beginning on Trump’s monumental arch

It is ironic that Mr. Trump alluded to his name not being on the ballot as the cause for the Republican collapse because, for many voters, the midterm election was indeed a referendum on the second Trump administration’s performance in office. The result has been an unambiguous thumbs-down from voters so far as top policy areas of the Trump administration are concerned, including cost of living and jobs, immigration enforcement, the war in Iran. The writing was on the wall, as were the approval ratings, especially in the case of oil prices and the Iran war, given that the price of gas in the U.S. has soared since the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz escalated. Similarly, the widespread raids by ICE and accelerated deportation processes for undocumented migrants led to protests across States and galvanised progressives around immigration reform. While Democrats may be justified in celebrating their victory after two years of harsh Trumpism, they would do well to remember that the President still retains a veto vote for policies passed by Congress. The temptation to launch a series of investigations and interrogate the functioning of the Trump White House may be strong, yet congressional Democrats may wish to avoid any posturing that yields no palpable policy impact, including kicking off impeachment proceedings against Mr. Trump. A more productive way forward for Democratic lawmakers would be to engage with the White House and, through negotiation and compromise, mitigate the real impact of deleterious policies in critical areas such as health-care insurance and tariffs.

articles.title: Danger in the sewer: On India’s sewer cleaning deaths
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.

Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme . And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

• The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

articles.title: Damning report: On Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Briefing the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last week on the International Commission of Inquiry’s latest report on the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories , its chairperson, retired Indian judge Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, did not couch his words in ambiguity. He said that the unequivocal conclusion was that Israeli security forces continued to commit “war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of genocide” a year after the October 2025 ceasefire agreement brokered by the U.S. The Commission’s third such submission since October 7, 2023, the report focuses on the “killings and bodily and mental harm by state actors”, predominantly Israeli security forces. It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers. Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.

The committee’s findings have shocked many around the world but have not thus far effected much action. The UNGA lacks the power to implement any resolution aimed at preventing Israel’s actions, and the UN Security Council lacks the consensus to do so, given the U.S.’s support of Israel. So, it should come as no surprise that Justice Muralidhar could not even present the report to the UNGA in person, as the U.S. withheld grant of a visa. New Delhi, while upholding Palestinian rights and providing humanitarian aid, has avoided any recommendation that could harm relations with Israel. India has abstained from UN resolutions calling for a ceasefire or action against Israel , while continuing to supply it with arms, ammunition, ordnance and drone parts. The Ministry of External Affairs has neither directly criticised Israel’s actions nor commented on the disturbing findings of reports by the UN commission chaired by Justice Muralidhar and his predecessor, 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navanethem Pillay . The government’s silence is in conflict with its stated principles and could place it on the wrong side of history.

articles.title: AQI slips to 'severe' in Delhi; Mumbai, Chennai wake up to smog morning after Deepavali
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Delhi Air Quality Index slips near “severe” mark as a thick layer of toxic haze engulfed India’s National capital on Monday (November 9, 2026). Despite stringent restrictions on fireworks imposed by the Supreme Court, people defied the deadline way past 10 p.m. on Deepavali night.
According to the Central Pollution Control Board Live Dashboard, Delhi AQI levels have gone up to 404 at 4 a.m. today and have been in respite since then.

Burari Crossing registered the highest reading at 441, followed by Vivek Vihar at 437, Delhi Technological University (DTU) at 434, North Campus of Delhi University and Jahangirpuri at 433 each, and Rohini at 430.
Beyond the National Capital, AQI also slumped in several other Indian cities. Mumbai saw hazy conditions, with a thick layer of smog blanketing the Kalanagar and Bandra areas as air quality worsened.

According to monitoring data, Kherwadi-Bandra East recorded an AQI of 264, followed by Sewri at 226, Ghatkopar at 221 and Chembur at 216. Byculla recorded an AQI of 193, Mindspace-Malad West 191, Kandivali West 187 and Worli 148. Kurla recorded an AQI of 96.
In Uttar Pradesh, a thick layer of smog blanketed Lucknow as several parts of the city woke up to hazy conditions.

Northern and western hubs bore the brunt of the pollution, with Lucknow (246), Amritsar (242), Jodhpur (234), Ahmedabad (230), Dehradun (228), Jaipur (223), Udaipur (223), and Surat (207) all slipping into the “poor” category.
Central and industrial belts similarly saw a spike in readings, including Nagpur (239), Pune (221), Bhopal (205), Mumbai (171) and Kolkata (167), exacerbated by Deepavali emissions.

Meanwhile, southern cities maintained relatively cleaner profiles, with Chennai standing at 208 (”poor”), while Bangalore (127), Hyderabad (120) and Thiruvananthapuram (67) recorded moderate-to-satisfactory air quality levels.
According to CPCB classification, an AQI between 0 and 50 is considered ‘good’, 51-100 ‘satisfactory’, 101-200 ‘moderate’, 201-300 ‘poor’, 301-400 ‘very poor’ and 401-500 ‘severe’.

With Stage III measures in force following the CAQM’s decision, existing restrictions will continue alongside additional pollution-control measures, increased enforcement and directions to concerned agencies to prevent further deterioration in air quality.

The emergency action plan applies across Delhi and adjoining districts of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan. It is invoked as a precautionary measure based on meteorological and pollution forecasts provided by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) and the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), allowing restrictions to be implemented before citywide AQI levels reach the ‘severe’ category.

fullParagraphs: Deepavali night (November 8, 2026) in Delhi saw air pollution levels in the national capital reach alarmingly high levels after firecrackers were burst across the city well past the Supreme Court-permitted hours on the festival. The national capital is under Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) with multiple restrictions in place.

A row has now been sparked after senior Congress leader Ajay Maken flagged the non-availability of PM 2.5 readings at 25 of Delhi’s 39 air quality monitoring stations on the night of Deepavali. He pointed out that air pollution levels at the national capital’s nine stations reached 38.4 times the World Health Organisation’s (WHO) 24-hour limit (as per available data)

Mr Maken, in a post on X, alleged discrepancies in the capital’s air pollution monitoring data, claiming that PM 2.5 readings in 25 stations were not recorded between 2 AM and 3 AM on the night of the festival.

Particulate matter, or particle pollution , is the general term for a mixture of solid particles and liquid droplets found in the air. There are two sizes of particulate matter (PM), i.e. PM 10 and PM 2.5.

articles.title: Hyderabad: Retired banker’s sketch puts Ladki-Ka-Pul’s one-way traffic plan in motion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A 73-year-old retired bank employee’s hand-drawn map has given Hyderabad Traffic Police an idea they are now seriously examining — a one-way traffic loop around Lakdi-ka-pul and Saifabad. What began as an email suggestion nearly a year ago has progressed to a traffic simulation study and inspections by senior police officers, even as the department explores similar arrangements at other congestion-prone locations across Hyderabad.

Palakodeti Chandrasekhar emailed the police with his proposal to reorganise traffic movement in the busy Lakdi-ka-pul stretch. He was subsequently invited to the Police Commissioner’s office, where he explained the idea. Mr. Chandrasekhar also submitted a hand-drawn map, marking the proposed directions of traffic with arrows.
“I am neither a police officer nor an engineer, and I am certainly no expert at drawing. I sketched the map to the best of my ability,” Mr. Chandrasekhar said.

The sketch maps a proposed loop connecting Lakdi-ka-pul, the Secretariat road, Ravindra Bharathi and the Old Saifabad Police Station, with landmarks such as Dwaraka Hotel, the LIC Building, the Assembly, Public Gardens and the DGP’s office marked along the route.
A view of traffic on Lakdi-ka-pul stretch in Hyderabad. File | Photo Credit: NAGARA GOPAL

Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic) D. Joel Davis said the police had conducted a simulation study to assess its feasibility. However, several road improvements would be necessary before even a trial could be introduced. “Certain intersections would have to be developed or modified to ensure smoother movement under the proposed arrangement,” said the officer.

Hyderabad Police Commissioner V.C. Sajjanar, accompanied by Mr. Davis; DCP Traffic-I Avinash Kumar; ACP Traffic Khairatabad Zone S. Mohan Kumar and Traffic Adviser Venkat Ramaiah, inspected stretches near Dwaraka Hotel, the Old Saifabad Police Station, HDFC, Iqbal Minar and Ravindra Bharathi to assess road conditions and existing traffic patterns.

Mr. Sajjanar said that one-way loops might require motorists to travel a few hundred metres extra, but could make journeys hassle-free, reduce honking and help curb pollution caused by congestion and vehicles remaining stationary with their engines running.

Referring to the one-way arrangement around KBR Park , he said the police had received considerable positive feedback from commuters, particularly about smoother movement and reduced honking. He said there was hardly any honking around KBR Park following the changes. “There were some hiccups initially, but I thank the people of Hyderabad for supporting the initiative. We look forward to better collaboration between the public and the police,” he said.
Hyderabad Police received positive feedback from people about one-way vehicular flow around Kasu Brahmananda Reddy (KBR) National Park in Hyderabad. File | Photo Credit: NAGARA GOPAL

In Cyberabad, officials are examining a separate loop connecting Biodiversity Junction, IKEA , Mindspace Rotary, Times Square Road, Knowledge City, Qualcomm, Dallas Centre Road and My Home Bhooja, before reconnecting with Biodiversity Junction.

Cyberabad Commissioner of Police M. Ramesh and Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Sunpreet Singh inspected the proposed corridor on November 6. Officials were asked to prepare a detailed traffic study covering bottlenecks, traffic generated by buildings and the availability and capacity of parking facilities.

articles.title: Keralam power purchase row: BJP leader V. Muraleedharan says CM must clarify if tenders were called
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national executive member and MLA V. Muraleedharan has asked Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan to clarify whether tenders were invited before the government opted to purchase power from GNA Energy, a digital over-the-counter (OTC) trading platform.

Stressing the need for transparency in the use of government funds at a press conference on Monday, Mr. Muraleedharan said the government should also clarify whether private companies other than GNA Energy had approached it and the rates offered by them.

The “power crisis” in the State, he said, was felt most acutely during peak hours, from 6 p.m. to midnight or 2 a.m. However, the agreement with GNA Energy was for the purchase of power round the clock, and not just during peak hours. According to experts, this would create an additional burden of ₹1,500 crore on the people, he said.

Mr. Muraleedharan asked whether the government would be willing to disclose a comparison of the peak-hour power supply offered by GNA Energy and the Himachal Pradesh government, along with the rates, “in a manner that can be understood by the layman.”

Keralam experienced the highest power shortage during April and May. However, the agreement with GNA Energy covered the period from November 2026 to March 2027. Negotiations for power purchases for April and May would see a further increase in rates. However, the rates offered by Himachal Pradesh covered the April-May period as well. “What is the rationale behind declining Himachal Pradesh’s offer and going with GNA Energy without inviting tenders?” the senior BJP leader asked.
If tenders were not invited, the government should clarify what other norms were followed in selecting GNA Energy, he added.

He also questioned why Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph was silent on the issue. “Does he have no stance on the issue? Usually, it is the Electricity Department that takes decisions on such matters. However, recently the Chief Minister has been making statements on the matter. Has the Electricity Minister gone on leave? Is the Chief Minister handling his portfolio?” Mr. Muraleedharan asked.
The MLA said there were suspicions that the Kerala State Electricity Regulatory Commission was being overruled when such decisions were made.
He also questioned why the United Democratic Front (UDF) government in Keralam was not entering into an agreement with another Congress-ruled State and was instead opting for GNA Energy.
The Chief Minister recently defended his decision to accept GNA Energy’s offer over a proposal from Himachal Pradesh, stating that the latter would entail an additional liability of ₹2,230 crore.

articles.title: Excess ethanol in petrol: Keralam launches random checks at pumps after Karnataka detects high levels
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: After sample testing in Karnataka revealed that petrol sold by several major oil companies in the State contained ethanol far above the prescribed 20% level , the Keralam government has also begun inspections in fuel outlets to check ethanol levels. Food and Civil Supplies Minister Anoop Jacob on Monday (November 9, 2026) announced random inspections at fuel outlets in four districts – Thiruvananthapuram, Ernakulam, Kozhikode and Kannur.

Thiruvananthapuram District Supply Officer Smitha S.R. told The Hindu that samples are being collected from two pumps in the district, which will be sent to a lab accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) for analysis.
“We have completed a sample collection from one of the pumps. Samples from one more pump will be collected today (Monday),” she said.

In samples collected in Karnataka, the level of ethanol in some cases was found to be as high as 31.2%, raising questions about transparency in the ethanol-blended petrol being sold to consumers across the country. The Commissioner of Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs as well as Taluk Supply Officers have the powers to conduct inspections and initiate legal action as per a 2014 notification issued by the State government.
Mr. Jacob said the sample analysis will be completed in a timebound manner, with results expected within 10 days.

He said the government decided to go ahead with the inspections considering the developments in Karnataka as well as the complaints and concerns raised by consumers regarding possible damage to their vehicles due to contaminated fuel.

fullParagraphs: Oil prices fell at Monday’s (November 9, 2026) open after U.S. President ​Donald Trump said he was highly unlikely to order new Iran ‌attackswhile talks to end the conflict make progress, despite both ​nations’ reports of attacks on ships in or near ⁠the Strait of Hormuz.
Brent was down 84 cents, or 0.85%, to $97.48 a barrel by 0138 GMT, while West Texas Intermediate fell 32 cents, or ‌0.35%, to $90.51 a barrel.

The fall reversed minor gains made on Friday’s (November 6, 2026) settlement as the market assessed the ‌possibility of further U.S. strikes on Iran, although Brent fell ‌17% ⁠last week, the steepest weekly drop since the start ⁠of the COVID pandemic and the biggest in absolute terms, according to LSEG data dating back to 1988.
“It depends on whether or not they sign ​a very strong agreement,” Trump ‌told CNN in a phone interview. “The answer is, highly unlikely it’s going to be necessary.”

Mr. Trump had hinted at renewing attacks on Iran after last week’s U.S. midterm elections , but there has ‌been no sign of a large-scale U.S. military operation. ​Iran has said it would respond by striking U.S. and Israeli targets.

Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM ⁠Trade, called Mr. Trump’s comments “more measured” but said “the market is still waiting to see whether the midterms have produced a lasting shift in Trump’s ‌approach to the conflict, or whether this is just another temporary change in tone.”

Oil is headed for a glut again as recovering West Asian oil flows, rising production from other countries and weak demand have pushed global supply above consumption, JPMorgan said in a report on Friday (November 6, 2026), estimating a surplus of 1.1 million barrels ‌per day in September, widening to 1.4 million bpd in October.

On Sunday (November 8, 2026), ​Iraq reached an understanding with the U.S. to allow Iraqi oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz via ⁠a shipping lane near Oman, Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said in an ⁠interview with Al Jazeera.
He said Iraq’s losses from the Iran war and disruptions to oil exports had reached $60 ‌billion.
Separately the Houthis claimed responsibility for an attack on Saudi Aramco’s offices in the capital Riyadh on Sunday that left windows ​blown out but no reported casualties.

articles.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

For a few weeks, Rampur, on the banks of the Sutlej river, comes alive with the fair (November 11-14 this year, with trading grounds open through the month), offering a sensory map of the Himalaya. Colourful textiles, yak wool, pashmina, dry fruits, agricultural produce, Kinnauri apples, indigenous crafts and precious stones fill the marketplace. Among its most captivating sights are the magnificent Chamurthi horses, the hardy “ships of the cold desert”.
Kinnauri weaves on sale at Lavi Fair. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala
At the Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, Shimla district. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala
Jewellery on sale at Lavi Fair. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala

Traders once travelled from Tibet, Nepal, Central Asia and Afghanistan. Tradition traces the fair’s origins to a 17th-century treaty between Raja Kehri Singh of Bushahr and Tibet, establishing it as a meeting point for traders, pilgrims and storytellers along the Silk Route. Though trans-Himalayan trade declined after Tibet’s occupation in 1959, the fair survived on the Buddhist circuit and was accorded international status by the Himachal Pradesh government.

Pratibha Singh, a member of the Rampur Bushahr royal family which founded the fair and continues to honour the tradition, recalls its legacy of pashmina and Kinnauri shawls, some woven over years, alongside trans-Himalayan textiles and local produce. The GI-tagged Kinnauri shawl, with bright geometric motifs, speaks its own language of colour: white for water, yellow for earth, red for fire, green for air, and blue for sky.

On my last visit, a group of elderly women from South India told me they discovered the fair through a fellow traveller whose husband was a biker in the 1990s. A friend from Odisha recalls how in the 90s, his ophthalmologist-father’s eye camps in Rampur led to lifelong friendships and an annual habit of sourcing Kinnauri apples and dry fruits.
Kinnauri apples on sale at Lavi Fair. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala
Traders at Lavi Fair accept payments via UPI now. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala

For Ami Chand Gautam, a Lavi trader since the 1980s, the fair tells a story of changing prices and livelihoods. He remembers when “ chilgoza , the rare pine nut gathered in Kinnaur’s upper reaches, sold for just ₹4-₹5 per kg, almost the price of rice then. Today, it fetches ₹14,000-15,000 per kg,” he says.
